features.title: Shared client crate and the dependency check
features.description: A new workspace crate `crates/custodio-client` holds only what both clients need and the client documentation will describe: the bus name, object path and interface name, the argument bounds (such as the largest `.p12`), and the calls to the service. It does not depend on `custodiod`. `custodio-cli` and `custodio-pkcs11` use it, and neither has `custodiod` as a normal or build dependency, directly or transitively, nor names `custodiod::` in its `src/`. Dev-dependencies that only host the service in tests are still allowed. Introduces the `just client-deps` recipe: it reads `cargo metadata` and fails on any such dependency or source reference. It has a negative control (a fixture manifest that depends on `custodiod` must fail) and runs inside `just lint`, so `just check` and CI enforce it (SPEC harness "Dependency check", acceptance 12).
features.verify: just check && just client-deps && ! grep -rq 'custodiod::' crates/custodio-cli/src crates/custodio-pkcs11/src && cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1 | python3 -I -c 'import json,sys; m=json.load(sys.stdin); sys.exit(0 if any(p["name"]=="custodio-client" for p in m["packages"]) else 1)'

features.title: D-Bus error names in the project's namespace
features.description: One service error type gives every failure a client must tell apart its own D-Bus error name, all under one prefix in the project's namespace (for example `com.rfirma.Custodio1.Error.`). At least these are distinct: invalid arguments, no such key, key id already taken, polkit denied, authorization unavailable, wrong password or unreadable `.p12`, unsupported key type, certificate does not match the key, audit unavailable, and internal or storage failure. The existing `ImportP12` and `Sign` return only these names, with no more `org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed`, `AccessDenied` or `InvalidArgs`. Message texts are fixed and never contain key material, a password, a path or a string that failed validation; a test feeds such values in and checks every message. The client crate exposes the names and the CLI chooses its text and exit status from the name, never from the message. Unit and integration tests whose names contain `error_name`. A new source file of the error type joins the `mutants` recipe.
features.verify: grep -q 'error_name' <(cargo test -p custodiod --locked -- --list 2>/dev/null) && just check && just test-integration && just mutants-diff F64

features.title: API contract check against the client documentation
features.description: `docs/client-api.md` gets a reference part that lists every method of `com.rfirma.Custodio1` with its arguments, D-Bus types, bounds and return values, every error name of F64, and every polkit action, in a fixed format a test can read. Introduces the `just api-contract` recipe, which also runs in `just test-integration` and in `just test`. It starts the service on a private bus with fake polkit and compares the document with the live introspection data (methods, arguments, properties), with the service's error type (error names), and with the shipped `.policy` file (actions), in both directions. Negative controls: copies of the document with an extra or a missing method, argument, error name or action must each fail. From here on every feature that changes the API updates this part in the same change (SPEC harness "API contract check", acceptance 12).
features.verify: just check && just api-contract

features.title: Research: how custodiod can read the caller's app-id
features.description: Settles the open question "How `custodiod` can read the app-id" with a section `## F66` in `docs/findings.md`. Each of options (a) to (d) is tried, or ruled out with its reason, under the shipped `data/custodio.service` on a supported target (in the e2e guest, for example debian13), with the commands run and their output. Candidates include reading `/.flatpak-info` through the `ProcessFD` pidfd, and the caller's cgroup (`app-flatpak-<id>-*.scope`) through anything the unit already allows. The section ends with one line `Decision:` naming the chosen source, or `(d)` when none works. It is never (a), which loosens the unit, nor (b), which is not built in M3. Changes only documents: the unit, the exposure gate and the code stay as they are.

features.title: Research: service detection through xdg-dbus-proxy
features.description: Settles the open question "Detection through the flatpak proxy" with a section `## F67` in `docs/findings.md`. From `xdg-dbus-proxy`'s filtering source (`flatpak-proxy.c`, cited by file and line at a named version), it says which bus-driver calls the proxy passes, filters or rewrites for a peer with `--system-talk-name=com.rfirma.Custodio1`: `NameHasOwner`, `ListActivatableNames`, `StartServiceByName`, `GetNameOwner` and `GetConnectionCredentials`, plus a direct call to the service. It also says what a sandboxed client sees when the service is absent, cannot be activated (`Exec=/bin/false`), or is not in its talk list. It ends with the detection steps the client documentation (F82) will give for the host and for a flatpak.

features.title: Key store kept apart per owner
features.description: The key store records the owner uid of every key and keeps each owner's keys apart on disk (for example one directory per uid), so a lookup by owner and id never reads another owner's entries and "another uid's key" and "no key" cannot differ by construction. Ids are unique per owner: two owners may each hold `my-key`. A key and its certificate are stored under the same owner, and list returns each key's id, type and certificate. The existing store rules apply to every new directory and file: exact modes, owner checks, no symlinks, refuse rather than repair, atomic writes that never overwrite silently. Two concurrent creates of the same owner and id leave exactly one key, and the other fails as already taken. There is no code for an earlier layout (SPEC section 4). Store layer only: F70 switches the service to it. Unit tests whose names contain `per_owner`, including the concurrency case; `data/tmpfiles.d` is updated if the layout needs it.
features.verify: grep -q 'per_owner' <(cargo test -p custodiod --locked -- --list 2>/dev/null) && just check && just mutants-diff F68

features.title: Store primitives for delete and certificate replacement
features.description: The owner-scoped store adds the two primitives that delete and replace certificate need. Replace certificate swaps a key's certificate atomically: a concurrent reader always sees the old one or the new one, never neither, and the key file is untouched. Delete first makes the key unusable (a lookup then reports no such key), then either commits (the key's files are removed from the state directory together) or restores the key exactly as it was. That is the order SPEC section 5 needs to submit the journal entry between the two. A lookup racing with a delete returns the whole key or no such key. All store rules still apply. Unit tests whose names contain `delete_key` and `replace_cert`, including concurrent readers.
features.verify: grep -q 'delete_key' <(cargo test -p custodiod --locked -- --list 2>/dev/null) && grep -q 'replace_cert' <(cargo test -p custodiod --locked -- --list 2>/dev/null) && just check && just mutants-diff F69

features.title: Caller-scoped import, list and sign in the service
features.description: The service uses the owner-scoped store. Import stores the key under the uid the bus reports for the calling connection, and no argument can set it. An import under an id another uid uses succeeds. List returns only the caller's keys, each with its id, key type and DER certificate in one call, replacing `ListKeys`/`ListCertificates` if the builder chooses one method. The PKCS#11 module's backend moves to the new list call in the same change, since it is the list's only consumer; nothing else of the module changes here. Sign looks the key up among the caller's keys before polkit. When the key is not there (missing, or another uid's), the call fails with the "no such key" name, polkit is not asked, and the journal behaves the same in both cases. A missing uid, or a failed `ProcessFD` cross-check, refuses every method as "authorization unavailable", list included: never an empty or unfiltered list. Root is a uid like any other. Integration tests with at least two caller uids, through the replaceable credentials interface, have names containing `other_uid`. The reference part of `docs/client-api.md` is updated. The ownership checks are covered by the `mutants` recipe (acceptances 1 and 2 at integration level).
features.verify: grep -q 'other_uid' <(cargo test -p custodiod --locked -- --list 2>/dev/null) && just check && just test-integration && just api-contract && just mutants-diff F70

features.title: polkit approval for import
features.description: Import asks polkit once per call, with `AllowUserInteraction`, under its own action (for example `com.rfirma.custodio.import`). The action is in the shipped policy, with `auth_self` on every defaults line, never a `_keep` variant, the owner annotation the signing action has, and its own dialog text. The order is: arguments and bounds, then whether the caller already has the id, then polkit, then decrypting the `.p12`. With polkit denying or unavailable, the call fails with the documented name and the state is unchanged, and the `.p12` decoder (behind a test double) was never called. After approval, a wrong password and an unsupported key each give their own name. A second call asks again, and nothing is cached. The policy test checks the new action's defaults and annotation. If a new policy file is added, all three packages ship it. Integration tests whose names contain `import_polkit`. `docs/client-api.md` is updated (acceptances 3 and 4 for import).
features.verify: grep -q 'import_polkit' <(cargo test -p custodiod --locked -- --list 2>/dev/null) && just check && just test-integration && just api-contract && just package && just package-parity && just mutants-diff F71

features.title: Journal entries name the operation; import entries
features.description: Every audit entry carries the operation (sign, import, and later delete and replace certificate) in a documented field, so an administrator can query by it, and existing signing entries stay valid under the compatibility rule of `docs/audit.md`. Every import that reaches authorization leaves exactly one entry once the outcome is known. It holds the caller's uid and pid, the key id, the key type when known, and the outcome, and never the `.p12`, its password or the certificate bytes (raw, hex or base64). An import whose entry cannot be submitted is not kept: the key is not in the store and the call fails as "audit unavailable". Refusals before authorization keep M1's behaviour. `docs/audit.md` documents the new field, outcomes and messages, with a query per operation, and its docs test covers them. Integration tests whose names contain `import_entry`.
features.verify: grep -q 'import_entry' <(cargo test -p custodiod --locked -- --list 2>/dev/null) && just check && just test-integration && just mutants-diff F72

features.title: Delete a key
features.description: A new method deletes one of the caller's keys with its certificate. Order: argument bounds, then lookup among the caller's keys (missing or another uid's: "no such key", no polkit, the same journal behaviour), then polkit once per call, with `AllowUserInteraction`, under its own delete action. Like the import action it has `auth_self` defaults, no `_keep`, the owner annotation and its own text. After approval the key is made unusable, the entry (operation delete) is submitted, and only then are the files removed. If the entry cannot be submitted, the key is restored and the call fails as "audit unavailable". Denied or unavailable polkit changes nothing. A sign racing with the delete either completes with the key or fails as "no such key". Afterwards the id can be imported again. `docs/client-api.md` and `docs/audit.md` are updated. Integration tests whose names contain `delete_call`, with two uids, the fake polkit counting calls and a failing audit sink (acceptances 1, 3, 6, 7 and 8 at integration level).
features.verify: grep -q 'delete_call' <(cargo test -p custodiod --locked -- --list 2>/dev/null) && grep -q 'other_uid' <(cargo test -p custodiod --locked -- --list 2>/dev/null) && just check && just test-integration && just api-contract && just package && just package-parity && just mutants-diff F73

features.title: Replace the certificate of a key
features.description: A new method takes a DER X.509 certificate for one of the caller's keys, with a documented size bound that is checked before any key, file or polkit is touched. Then: lookup among the caller's keys (missing or another uid's: "no such key", no polkit), parsing, and the check that the certificate's public key is the key's own. The certificate is only parsed and compared: no chain, revocation or date check. A mismatch fails with "certificate does not match the key" and changes nothing. polkit is asked once per call under its own replace-certificate action, with the same defaults and annotation rules as import. After approval the certificate is swapped atomically, and the key is untouched. If the entry (operation replace certificate, no certificate bytes) cannot be submitted, the old certificate stays and the call fails as "audit unavailable". After a replace, list returns the new certificate. Which of parsing and polkit comes first is the builder's choice, documented in `docs/client-api.md`. `docs/audit.md` is updated. Integration tests whose names contain `replace_cert_call` (acceptances 1, 3, 5, 7 and 8 at integration level).
features.verify: grep -q 'replace_cert_call' <(cargo test -p custodiod --locked -- --list 2>/dev/null) && just check && just test-integration && just api-contract && just package && just package-parity && just mutants-diff F74

features.title: Fuzz targets for the new arguments and for certificate input
features.description: The `dbus_args` fuzz target covers the argument parsing of every method of the API, delete and replace certificate included. A new target `cert_input` feeds arbitrary bytes to the certificate parsing and key-match check of replace certificate. Introduces the `just fuzz-smoke` recipe: it runs every fuzz target of the repository for a fixed number of runs with a fixed seed, and fails on a crash. It joins `just nightly`, so CI runs it.
features.verify: test -f crates/custodiod/fuzz/fuzz_targets/cert_input.rs && just check && just fuzz-build && just lint-fuzz && just fuzz-smoke

features.title: App-id state in journal entries, from a replaceable source
features.description: Every entry of sign, import, delete and replace certificate says one of three things: an app-id was read (and names it), the caller has no flatpak info, or the app-id could not be determined. The values are documented in `docs/audit.md` under its compatibility rule. The value comes from a replaceable source interface that is given the caller's pinned process. A value is copied into the entry only if it is a valid flatpak application id; any other value is never copied anywhere (entry, log or error). Reading has a documented time bound: a source that never returns leaves "could not be determined" within the bound. Stuck reads are capped, so they cannot exhaust the service's threads or memory. The app-id never changes the outcome or the polkit question. Integration tests with a fake source whose names contain `app_id` cover the three cases, an invalid id and a source that never returns. The app-id validation is covered by the `mutants` recipe (acceptance 9 at integration level).
features.verify: grep -q 'app_id' <(cargo test -p custodiod --locked -- --list 2>/dev/null) && just check && just test-integration && just mutants-diff F76

features.title: The real app-id source decided by F66
features.description: Implements the source chosen in the `Decision:` line of `docs/findings.md` section F66. For `/.flatpak-info`, it is read as the process pinned by `ProcessFD` sees it, and the service confirms afterwards that the process is still the same. Symlinks are not followed, only a regular file of bounded size is read, a FIFO, device or slow filesystem cannot block beyond the F76 bound, and the application name comes from a strict parser. Under (c) the same rules apply to that source instead. Unit tests use real hostile files (symlink, FIFO, oversized file, malformed text, invalid id), and the parser has the fuzz target `crates/custodiod/fuzz/fuzz_targets/app_id_source.rs`. The unit, `just security-score` and `just unit-hardening` stay as they are. If F66 decided (d), this feature instead records the deviation in `SPEC_DEVIATIONS.md` under `## F77`, amending acceptances 9 and 15 so the entry always says "could not be determined", and the production source returns that.
features.verify: { grep -q '^## F77' SPEC_DEVIATIONS.md || test -f crates/custodiod/fuzz/fuzz_targets/app_id_source.rs; } && just check && just test-integration && just fuzz-build && just fuzz-smoke && just mutants-diff F77

features.title: PKCS#11 module on the new API, with two uids
features.description: The module talks to the service only through `custodio-client` and the documented API, and tells failures apart only by error name. A process sees as tokens only its own uid's keys. After a replace certificate the token exposes the new certificate, and a signature made afterwards verifies against it. After a delete the key's token is gone. With the service absent there are still no slots. Every M1 and M2 module guarantee stays: a connection per call, fork safety, no thread left behind. The `cryptoki` integration tests gain cases whose names contain `other_uid`, `replace_cert` and `delete_key` (acceptances 1, 5 and 6 for the module).

Every CLI command, `import` included, shows failures from the documented error names, never from the message text, and exits non-zero on failure; usage errors keep their own status. features.title: `custodio delete` with terminal confirmation
features.description: `custodio delete <id>` asks on the terminal for confirmation, saying the key cannot be recovered, before it calls the service. polkit then asks too. Declining either one deletes nothing and exits non-zero. No flag skips the confirmation, and without a terminal the command refuses. The man page documents `delete`. Tests whose names contain `cli_delete` drive the prompt through a pty, against the service on a private bus with the fake polkit approving or denying (acceptance 11 for delete).

features.title: pkttyagent for import and delete without a graphical agent
features.description: When stdin is a terminal and no polkit agent answers for the session, `custodio import` and `custodio delete` start `pkttyagent` registered for the CLI's own process only, as `systemctl` does (for example `--process <own pid> --fallback`). They stop it when the call returns, on every path, errors included. The CLI never registers an agent for another process or for the whole session. Without a terminal it starts none. Tests whose names contain `pkttyagent` use a stub `pkttyagent` on `PATH` that records its arguments and lifetime, and check the process subject, that it is stopped, and that no agent starts without a tty (acceptance 11, pkttyagent part).
